speaker: Narendra Modi
quote_english: If even once, the money hoarded by these crooks in banks abroad, even if we bring only that back, every poor Indian would get free of cost Rs 15 to Rs 20 lakhs, just like that.
summary: Modi's campaign remark was a conditional illustration of how large black money abroad might be, not a literal pledge of Rs 15 lakh per account; no such deposits have been made and no estimate supporting the figure has been produced.

analysis:
BOOM traces the earliest mention to a 7 November 2013 rally at Kanker, where Modi said that if the black money held abroad were brought back, every poor Indian could get Rs 15-20 lakh. Fact-checkers read this as a hypothetical about the size of the hoard, not a promise to deposit money in each account. The English wording above is BOOM's rendering; no Hindi original or video was located.

On 5 February 2015 Amit Shah told ABP News that '15 lakhs will not be credited in anyone's account' and called it a 'jumla'/metaphor. The Congress called this an admission and demanded an apology. The phrase 'chunavi jumla' appears in a NewsGram paraphrase of Shah's words, not in the direct quotes seen.

No cash transfer of the kind alleged has occurred. The Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) Act was passed in 2015 (referred to in the 8 Nov 2016 speech text), but recovered amounts against any estimate were not retrieved here, so the ledger does not assess how much black money was actually brought back. The verdict reflects that the popular 'promise' framing overstates what was said, while the underlying illustration of recoverable wealth has not materialised.
notes: Verdict is a judgment call between 'misleading' (popular framing) and 'unachieved' (if the hypothetical is read as an aim). Hindi original, video and other 2014 rally variants not found. Black money recovery data (Black Money Act assessments, Swiss data) not retrieved. Quint fact-check page not opened; the Factly details come from search summary.
